facts.statement: Fossils of Erliansaurus were discovered near Sanhangobi in Inner Mongolia in 1999.
facts.quote: The remains of Erliansaurus were found near Sanhangobi in Inner Mongolia in 1999.

facts.statement: The type species Erliansaurus bellamanus was described by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2002.
facts.quote: The type species, Erliansaurus bellamanus, was described by Xu Xing, Zhang Xiaohong, Paul Sereno, Zhao Xijin, Kuang Xuewen, Han Jun and Tan Lin in 2002.

facts.statement: The specific name bellamanus means "beautiful hand" in Latin, referencing the exquisite preservation of the forelimb.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the town of Erlian, and the specific name is derived from Latin bellus, "beautiful", and manus, "hand", in reference to the exquisite preservation of the forelimb.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, LH V0002, comes from the Santonian stage of the Iren Dabasu Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, LH V0002, was uncovered in the Iren Dabasu Formation dating from the Santonian stage.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton of a subadult that includes vertebrae, a scapula, a partial forelimb, pelvic fragments, leg bones, and partial foot bones, but lacks any skull traces.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton belonging to a subadult individual. It includes two cervical, one dorsal and two caudal vertebrae; a right scapula; a left forelimb only lacking the carpus; a partial right ilium and a fragmented ischium and pubis; the right femur; both tibiae, a right fibula and partial metatarsals. No skull traces were found.

facts.statement: Erliansaurus was a small to medium-sized therizinosaur estimated to be between 2.6 and 4 meters long and weighing between 91 and 400 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a small to medium-sized therizinosaur with an estimated length from 2.6 to 4 m and a weight of 91 to 400 kg.

facts.statement: The preserved left arm features enormous, strongly recurved and pointed claws, with the thumb claw being the largest, though the carpal bones are missing.
facts.quote: The left arm is exceptionally preserved with almost every element intact, its hands bore enormous, strongly recurved and pointed claws of which the thumb claw was the largest, however, the carpal bones are missing.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Erliansaurus to Therizinosauroidea in a basal position, suggesting it was likely not a therizinosaurid.
facts.quote: Erliansaurus was by the describers assigned to the Therizinosauroidea, in a basal position and likely not a therizinosaurid.

facts.statement: Some early cladistic analyses recovered Erliansaurus as a basal member of the Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: Some early cladistic analyses however, have recovered it as a basal member of the Therizinosauridae.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Erliansaurus within the family Therizinosauridae.
Fossil evidence places Erliansaurus in the Campanian stage, ranging from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Erliansaurus, meaning "Erlian lizard", is a therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85 to 68 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Erliansaurus (meaning "Erlian lizard") is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, around 85–68 million years ago, in the Iren Dabasu Formation, now near Erenhot, Inner Mongolia.
